title: Inflationary magnetogenesis from non-minimal coupling in large- and small-field potentials
summary: We investigate inflationary magnetogenesis in a scenario where conformal invariance of electromagnetism is broken through a \emph{non-minimal Yukawa-like coupling between the inflaton and the Ricci scalar}. We account for electromagnetic backreaction and the Schwinger effect, analyzing both standard single-field inflation and a generalized K-essence framework, \emph{dubbed quasi-quintessence}. We consider inflationary potentials compatible with Planck satellite constraints, including Starobinsky and $α$-attractor models for large fields, as well as hilltop scenarios for small fields. Moreover, we explore very different functional electromagnetic couplings, introducing a novel ansatz modeled for small-fields. We show that the non-minimal coupling plays a central role in controlling the dynamics, \emph{acting as a timing parameter that regulates the onset of electric backreaction and the Schwinger regime}. This leads to a deep modification of the magnetogenesis process. Indeed, the amplitude of the generated magnetic fields can be enhanced by several orders of magnitude with respect to the minimally coupled case, reaching present-day values up to $B_0 \sim 10^{-13}\,\mathrm{G}$ in large-field scenarios, \emph{which appear as the only ones compatible with observational bounds}. Conversely, small-field models yield negligible magnetic amplitudes and appear non-predictive within our non-minimal framework.

AI.tldr: Non-minimal Yukawa-like coupling between inflaton and Ricci scalar enhances inflationary magnetogenesis, with large-field models achieving B₀ ~ 10⁻¹³ G while small-field models yield negligible magnetic fields.
AI.motivation: To investigate inflationary magnetogenesis scenarios where conformal invariance of electromagnetism is broken through non-minimal coupling between inflaton and Ricci scalar, accounting for electromagnetic backreaction and Schwinger effect.
AI.method: Analyze both standard single-field inflation and generalized K-essence (quasi-quintessence) frameworks with inflationary potentials compatible with Planck constraints (Starobinsky, α-attractor for large fields, hilltop for small fields). Introduce novel ansatz for electromagnetic couplings in small-field scenarios. Study non-minimal coupling as timing parameter regulating electric backreaction and Schwinger regime.
AI.result: Non-minimal coupling enhances magnetic field amplitudes by several orders of magnitude compared to minimally coupled case, reaching B₀ ~ 10⁻¹³ G in large-field scenarios. Large-field models are the only ones compatible with observational bounds. Small-field models yield negligible magnetic amplitudes and appear non-predictive within this framework.
AI.conclusion: Non-minimal Yukawa-like coupling between inflaton and Ricci scalar plays central role in controlling magnetogenesis dynamics, acting as timing parameter that regulates backreaction and Schwinger effects. This significantly modifies magnetogenesis process, with large-field inflationary scenarios being observationally viable while small-field models are not predictive in this framework.

title: An Analytic Formalism of Inflation for Derivative Coupled Scalar Field and Validating its predictions for Some Inflationary Potentials
summary: One of the fundamental objectives of contemporary cosmology is to understand the physics of the inflationary universe, owing to its observably verifiable predictions about the very early universe with an energy scale of $\sim 10^{16}$ GeV. Recent observations from the ACT and the Planck mission, constrain the values of the scalar spectral index, $n_s$, and the tensor-to-scalar ratio, with state-of-the-art accuracy and upper limits, respectively. In the current work, a type of non minimally coupled inflationary model in which the gravity and the background scalar field interact through a covariant product of the Ricci tensor and derivatives of the scalar field. With this interaction at the backdrop, we estimate $n_s$ and $r$ for a wide range of inflaton self-interaction potentials, including power law, exponential $α$ attractor, Arctan, Hilltop, and polynomial model. We show that the higher derivative terms involving the scalar field resulting from the derivative coupling term can be handled without facing any singularity within the slow-roll regime. We show that it is possible to produce $n_s$ and $r$ values consistent with ACT and Planck observations for each of the chosen sets of potentials for the derivative coupled action.

AI.tldr: Non-minimally coupled inflationary model with derivative coupling between gravity and scalar field produces n_s and r values consistent with ACT and Planck observations for various inflaton potentials.
AI.motivation: To understand inflationary physics at ~10^16 GeV scale and reconcile theoretical predictions with precise observational constraints from ACT and Planck missions on scalar spectral index (n_s) and tensor-to-scalar ratio (r).
AI.method: Develop non-minimally coupled inflationary model with derivative coupling between Ricci tensor and scalar field derivatives. Analyze higher derivative terms within slow-roll regime without singularities. Test with multiple inflaton potentials: power law, exponential α attractor, Arctan, Hilltop, and polynomial models.
AI.result: Higher derivative terms from derivative coupling can be handled without singularities in slow-roll regime. Model produces n_s and r values consistent with ACT and Planck observations for all tested inflaton potentials.
AI.conclusion: Derivative-coupled inflationary models provide viable framework compatible with current observational constraints across diverse inflaton potential types, offering new approach to inflationary cosmology.

title: Low-ionization Metal Absorption at $0.7 \lesssim z \lesssim 2$ Confronting Cosmological Simulations with Observations
summary: Low-ionization metal absorption lines provide a primary probe of cool gas in and around galaxies. We confront observations of metal-line absorption in quasar spectra with predictions from the IllustrisTNG cosmological simulation in order to benchmark how well current galaxy formation models reproduce the observed circumgalactic medium (CGM) and intergalactic medium (IGM) absorption signatures. We implement two ionization prescriptions: a purely collisional model and a model including photo-ionization by a uniform ultraviolet background (UVB). Using a grid-based framework, we compute MgI, MgII and FeII column densities and construct column density probability distribution functions (PDFs) and equivalent width (EW) statistics for comparison with observations. The observational samples considered here are based on the High Resolution Echelle Spectrometer (HIRES), the Ultraviolet and Visual Echelle Spectrograph (UVES), the Sloan Digital Sky Survey (SDSS) and the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI). The computed PDFs broadly reproduce the observed ones across the sampled column density range of $10^{11.4}\lesssim \text{N}\lesssim 10^{16}\ \rm{cm^{-2}}$, indicating that the simulation captures the dominant physical drivers of low-ionization absorption. We then compute the cosmic incidence of MgII systems, namely the evolution of their number with redshift $d\mathcal{N}/{dz}$. The model that includes UVB accurately produces $d\mathcal{N}/{dz}$ up to equivalent widths (EW) of $\rm W_0^{2796} < 0.6\ \mathring{A}$, consistent with low-density photo-ionized gas in the outer CGM. At high EWs of $\rm W_0^{2796} > 1\ \mathring{A}$ TNG underestimates $d\mathcal{N}/{dz}$ and fails to capture its rise toward $z\sim2$.

AI.tldr: The paper compares low-ionization metal absorption line observations from quasar spectra with IllustrisTNG cosmological simulations, finding that the simulation broadly reproduces observed column density distributions but underestimates the cosmic incidence of strong MgII absorbers at high redshifts.
AI.motivation: To benchmark current galaxy formation models against observational data of low-ionization metal absorption lines in the circumgalactic and intergalactic media, assessing how well cosmological simulations reproduce observed absorption signatures.
AI.method: Used IllustrisTNG cosmological simulation with two ionization prescriptions (collisional-only and including uniform UVB photo-ionization). Computed MgI, MgII, and FeII column densities using grid-based framework, constructed column density PDFs and equivalent width statistics for comparison with observations from HIRES, UVES, SDSS, and DESI.
AI.result: The simulation broadly reproduces observed column density PDFs across the sampled range (10^11.4 to 10^16 cm^-2), indicating it captures dominant physical drivers of low-ionization absorption. The UVB-inclusive model accurately produces cosmic incidence of MgII systems up to EW < 0.6 Å, but underestimates incidence at high EWs (>1 Å) and fails to capture its rise toward z~2.
AI.conclusion: IllustrisTNG successfully reproduces observed low-ionization absorption signatures for moderate column densities, suggesting it captures key physical processes in the CGM/IGM. However, discrepancies at high equivalent widths indicate missing physics or limitations in modeling strong absorbers, particularly at higher redshifts.

title: Gas-rich ultra-diffuse galaxies: alleviating the MOND tension with HMG
summary: Gas-rich ultra-diffuse galaxies (UDGs) are an unusually sharp test for gravity models tied to the baryonic Tully--Fisher relation because several systems appear to rotate too slowly for their baryonic masses. This study revisits the six isolated gas-rich UDGs analysed by Mancera Piña et al. with the current outer-radius prescription of hyperconical modified gravity (HMG), using the published baryonic masses and circular velocities at the outer radii. The scan over the neighbourhood-scale parameter drives the model towards the asymptotic branch of HMG. For that limit, the HMG velocities are still systematically high for four of the six galaxies. Relative to the observed values, the fixed asymptotic branch gives $χ^2\simeq18.1$ for six objects, whereas Newtonian baryons alone give $χ^2\simeq9.7$, but MOND interpolation is much worse ($χ^2\simeq 615.7$). Using combined uncertainties, the per-galaxy HMG tension ranges from $0.2σ$ to $2.1σ$, very similar to the $0.1σ$ to $1.7σ$ found for Newtonian baryons, and much smaller than the $3.7σ$ to $5.9σ$ obtained for MOND. We conclude that the present outer-radius HMG implementation alleviates the difficulties of MOND, but is still not sufficient to account for the published central values of the UDG sample. Gas-rich UDGs therefore provide a useful discriminant between MOND and HMG.

AI.tldr: HMG gravity model reduces but doesn't fully resolve rotation discrepancies in gas-rich UDGs compared to MOND, providing a discriminant between modified gravity theories.
AI.motivation: Gas-rich ultra-diffuse galaxies (UDGs) challenge gravity models tied to the baryonic Tully-Fisher relation, as several systems rotate too slowly for their baryonic masses, making them sharp tests for modified gravity theories.
AI.method: Revisits six isolated gas-rich UDGs using hyperconical modified gravity (HMG) with current outer-radius prescription, scanning over neighbourhood-scale parameter to drive model toward asymptotic branch, comparing with Newtonian baryons and MOND using published baryonic masses and circular velocities.
AI.result: HMG velocities remain systematically high for four of six galaxies; HMG gives χ²≈18.1 vs Newtonian baryons χ²≈9.7, while MOND performs much worse (χ²≈615.7). HMG tension ranges 0.2σ-2.1σ per galaxy, similar to Newtonian baryons (0.1σ-1.7σ), much smaller than MOND (3.7σ-5.9σ).
AI.conclusion: Current outer-radius HMG implementation alleviates MOND's difficulties but insufficient to account for published central values of UDG sample; gas-rich UDGs provide useful discriminant between MOND and HMG.

title: Reionization Topology as a Probe of Self-Interacting Dark Matter
summary: We introduce a framework connecting dark matter self-interactions (SIDM) to the large-scale topology of cosmic reionization in this paper. SIDM core formation reduces the gas binding energy in high-$z$ halos, enhancing supernova-driven clearing of ionizing-photon escape channels. We decompose the observable signatures into two scale-dependent levers a percent-level shift in the emissivity-weighted halo bias $b_γ$ that modifies large-scale 21\,cm power, and a factor of 2--4 suppression of emissivity shot noise from increased duty cycles that reshapes intermediate-scale ionization morphology. We derive analytic predictions for the 21\,cm power spectrum ratio and validate them with a halo-by-halo semi-numerical excursion-set framework at $128^3$ resolution where individual halo duty-cycle stochasticity is resolved. For $σ/m = 1$--$10\;\mathrm{cm^2/g}$, we find $\sim 60$--$80\%$ suppression of emissivity shot-noise power, a $12$--$21\%$ reduction in the emissivity variance ratio $\langle \dot{N}^2\rangle/\langle\dot{N}\rangle^2$, and a $50$--$110\%$ increase in the Euler characteristic of the ionization field at fixed $\bar{x}_{\rm HI} = 0.5$. SIDM produces more numerous, more uniformly distributed HII bubbles compared to CDM's topology of fewer large bubbles around rare bright sources. Theintermediate scale signatures are potentially detectable by SKA1-Low in $\sim 1000$ hours. Our results establish reionization topology as a new, complementary probe of dark matter microphysics at mass scales $M \sim 10^{10}$--$10^{11}\,M_\odot$ and redshifts $z \sim 6$--$10$.

AI.tldr: SIDM affects cosmic reionization topology by enhancing gas clearing in halos, leading to more uniform HII bubble distribution and detectable 21cm power spectrum signatures.
AI.motivation: To establish cosmic reionization topology as a new probe of dark matter microphysics, specifically self-interacting dark matter (SIDM), by connecting SIDM effects on halo structure to observable signatures in the 21cm power spectrum and ionization morphology.
AI.method: Developed a framework connecting SIDM self-interactions to reionization topology, using analytic predictions for 21cm power spectrum ratios and validating with a halo-by-halo semi-numerical excursion-set framework at 128³ resolution that resolves individual halo duty-cycle stochasticity.
AI.result: For σ/m = 1-10 cm²/g: 60-80% suppression of emissivity shot-noise power, 12-21% reduction in emissivity variance ratio, 50-110% increase in Euler characteristic of ionization field at fixed neutral fraction. SIDM produces more numerous, uniformly distributed HII bubbles compared to CDM's fewer large bubbles around rare bright sources.
AI.conclusion: Reionization topology provides a new complementary probe of dark matter microphysics at mass scales M ∼ 10¹⁰-10¹¹ M⊙ and redshifts z ∼ 6-10, with intermediate-scale signatures potentially detectable by SKA1-Low in ∼1000 hours.

title: A first empirical derivation of the average dust attenuation law at 2<z<7
comment: 16 pages. Submitted to Astronomy and Astrophysics
summary: Dust attenuation strongly affects the observed spectral energy distributions of galaxies, introducing significant uncertainties in the derivation of key physical properties such as star formation rates, stellar masses, and metallicities. While attenuation curves have been extensively studied in the local Universe and at intermediate redshift, direct spectroscopic constraints at earlier cosmic epochs have remained limited prior to JWST. We aim to derive the average dust attenuation law of star-forming galaxies over the redshift range 2<z<7. We combine NIRSpec spectroscopy from the JADES survey with deep multi-wavelength photometry from the ASTRODEEP catalogs. Using a mass-selected sample (log(M_\star/M_\odot) > 9) of 120 galaxies with reliable Balmer decrement (Ha/Hb), we construct stacked spectral energy distributions in bins of Balmer optical depth and derive the selective attenuation curve following the empirical methodology introduced by Calzetti et al. (2000). The wavelength coverage is further extended toward the near-infrared using MIRI photometry. The resulting attenuation curve spans the rest-frame range 0.16-1.14mu and is well described by a smooth function. We derive a normalization factor R_V=3.98, finding that the average attenuation law is consistent with the local starburst relation in both slope and normalization. Compared to several determinations at intermediate redshift, however, our curve appears systematically flatter in the ultraviolet. We find no significant evidence for a 2175A UV bump in the average attenuation curve. Our results provide the first empirical determination of the average dust attenuation law for star-forming galaxies at 2<z<7 based on JWST spectroscopy. Despite the diversity of attenuation properties observed in individual systems, the ensemble-average behavior remains consistent with the local starburst relation.

AI.tldr: First empirical determination of average dust attenuation law for star-forming galaxies at 2<z<7 using JWST spectroscopy, finding consistency with local starburst relation but flatter UV slope than intermediate-redshift determinations.
AI.motivation: Dust attenuation introduces significant uncertainties in deriving key galaxy properties (star formation rates, stellar masses, metallicities). While extensively studied locally and at intermediate redshift, direct spectroscopic constraints at earlier cosmic epochs (z>2) have been limited prior to JWST.
AI.method: Combined NIRSpec spectroscopy from JADES survey with deep multi-wavelength photometry from ASTRODEEP catalogs. Used mass-selected sample (log(M*/M⊙)>9) of 120 galaxies with reliable Balmer decrement (Hα/Hβ). Constructed stacked spectral energy distributions in bins of Balmer optical depth and derived selective attenuation curve following Calzetti et al. (2000) empirical methodology. Extended wavelength coverage to near-infrared using MIRI photometry.
AI.result: Derived attenuation curve spanning rest-frame 0.16-1.14μm, well described by smooth function with normalization factor R_V=3.98. Average attenuation law consistent with local starburst relation in both slope and normalization. Curve appears systematically flatter in UV compared to intermediate-redshift determinations. No significant evidence for 2175Å UV bump in average attenuation curve.
AI.conclusion: First empirical determination of average dust attenuation law for star-forming galaxies at 2<z<7 based on JWST spectroscopy. Despite diversity in individual systems, ensemble-average behavior remains consistent with local starburst relation, providing crucial constraints for high-redshift galaxy studies.

title: On the origin of the BAOtr-DESI tension
summary: The fiducial-independent transversal BAO dataset (BAOtr) systematically prefers smaller comoving distance ratios $D_{\rm M}/r_{\rm d}$ than the DESI DR2 three-dimensional BAO measurements at $z \lesssim 0.65$, driving dataset-dependent CPL dark-energy inferences and conflicting conclusions about the Hubble tension. We investigate whether this disagreement can be attributed to the $Λ$CDM fiducial assumed in the 3D BAO pipeline, or resolved within the CPL parametrisation. We show that the published 3D BAO distances are fiducial-independent by construction, with residual effects at $\lesssim 0.3\%$ -- negligible against the 10--18\% BAOtr uncertainties. We then scan the CPL parameter space with $Ω_m$ and $H_0$ jointly determined at each $(w_0, w_a)$ by the Planck $θ_*$ constraint and optimisation against the DESI data. Two complementary tests are performed: a direct comparison of each DESI-optimized model with the BAOtr data, and an $α$-interpolation test that anchors the prediction to the DESI measurements. Both reveal an inescapable trade-off: models that fit DESI well ($χ^2_{\rm DESI} \lesssim 5$) yield $χ^2_{\rm BAOtr} \gtrsim 42$, while reducing the BAOtr tension to $χ^2_{\rm BAOtr} \sim 37$ requires $χ^2_{\rm DESI} \gtrsim 8$. No CMB-consistent CPL model fits both datasets simultaneously. The direct comparison at $z = 0.510$ -- where BAOtr and DESI disagree by $3.7σ$ (data-versus-data) -- sets an irreducible tension floor that no smooth modification of $D_{\rm M}(z)$ can remove. These conclusions are robust across analysis methods, extrapolation schemes, and substitution of SDSS for DESI. The remaining explanations are observational systematics -- most plausibly in the angular BAO measurements -- or new physics beyond CPL.

AI.tldr: BAOtr data systematically prefers smaller comoving distance ratios than DESI 3D BAO measurements at low redshifts, creating dataset-dependent dark energy inferences and conflicting conclusions about the Hubble tension. The study shows this tension cannot be resolved by ΛCDM fiducial assumptions or within the CPL parametrization, pointing to observational systematics or new physics beyond CPL.
AI.motivation: To investigate the disagreement between fiducial-independent transversal BAO (BAOtr) measurements and DESI DR2 three-dimensional BAO measurements at z ≲ 0.65, which leads to dataset-dependent CPL dark-energy inferences and conflicting conclusions about the Hubble tension. The study aims to determine whether this tension can be attributed to ΛCDM fiducial assumptions in the 3D BAO pipeline or resolved within the CPL parametrization.
AI.method: 1) Demonstrate that published 3D BAO distances are fiducial-independent by construction with residual effects < 0.3%. 2) Scan CPL parameter space with Ω_m and H_0 jointly determined at each (w_0, w_a) by Planck θ* constraint and optimization against DESI data. 3) Perform two complementary tests: direct comparison of each DESI-optimized model with BAOtr data, and α-interpolation test that anchors predictions to DESI measurements. 4) Test robustness across analysis methods, extrapolation schemes, and substitution of SDSS for DESI.
AI.result: 1) Models fitting DESI well (χ²_DESI ≲ 5) yield χ²_BAOtr ≳ 42, while reducing BAOtr tension to χ²_BAOtr ∼ 37 requires χ²_DESI ≳ 8. 2) No CMB-consistent CPL model fits both datasets simultaneously. 3) Direct comparison at z = 0.510 shows BAOtr and DESI disagree by 3.7σ (data-versus-data), setting an irreducible tension floor that no smooth modification of D_M(z) can remove. 4) Conclusions are robust across analysis methods, extrapolation schemes, and substitution of SDSS for DESI.
AI.conclusion: The tension between BAOtr and DESI BAO measurements cannot be resolved by ΛCDM fiducial assumptions or within the CPL parametrization. The remaining explanations are observational systematics (most plausibly in angular BAO measurements) or new physics beyond CPL. The irreducible tension at z = 0.510 suggests fundamental incompatibility between the datasets within current cosmological frameworks.

title: Magnetic field alignment with dense cores in the transition between cloud and core scales
summary: In a magnetically-dominated model of star formation, we expect to see alignments between the magnetic field orientation of star-forming dense cores and the cloud-scale magnetic field. Pandhi et al. (2023) showed instead, however, that the orientation of cores and their angular momentum vectors appear random with respect to the larger-scale magnetic field, implying that magnetic fields may play a diminished role in core formation and evolution. Here, we use higher-resolution dust polarization data from the B-Fields In Star-forming Region Observations (BISTRO) survey on the James Clerk Maxwell Telescope (JCMT) to investigate the change in the magnetic field orientation from cloud scales to core scales, and reassess any correlations between core-scale magnetic fields, core orientations and core velocity gradients. We produce a catalog of 79 cores over 14 star-forming regions with averaged core-scale magnetic field orientations. We find that the core-scale magnetic field is more disordered compared to the cloud-scale field, as measured by an increased standard deviation in the magnetic field vector orientations. Alignment between the core-scale and cloud-scale field varies greatly between regions. Our results are consistent with random alignments between the core-scale magnetic field, core orientation, and core velocity gradient, in agreement with the results by Pandhi et al. (2023) for the cloud-scale field. We conclude that there is a clear change in the magnetic field in the transition from cloud- to core-scales. Our results suggest that the magnetic field may not play a dominant role in the evolution of dense cores on core scales.

AI.tldr: Higher-resolution BISTRO survey data shows core-scale magnetic fields are more disordered than cloud-scale fields, with random alignments between core-scale fields, core orientations, and velocity gradients, suggesting magnetic fields may not dominate dense core evolution.
AI.motivation: To investigate the discrepancy between magnetically-dominated star formation models (predicting alignment between core and cloud-scale magnetic fields) and Pandhi et al. (2023) findings showing random orientations, using higher-resolution BISTRO data to reassess magnetic field correlations from cloud to core scales.
AI.method: Used higher-resolution dust polarization data from BISTRO survey on JCMT to analyze magnetic field orientation changes from cloud to core scales. Produced catalog of 79 cores across 14 star-forming regions with averaged core-scale magnetic field orientations, comparing core-scale magnetic fields, core orientations, and core velocity gradients.
AI.result: Core-scale magnetic fields are more disordered than cloud-scale fields (increased standard deviation in orientations). Alignment between core-scale and cloud-scale fields varies greatly between regions. Results show random alignments between core-scale magnetic field, core orientation, and core velocity gradient, consistent with Pandhi et al. (2023) findings for cloud-scale field.
AI.conclusion: Clear change in magnetic field structure occurs in transition from cloud to core scales. Magnetic fields may not play a dominant role in dense core evolution on core scales, challenging magnetically-dominated star formation models.

title: First observational constraints on cosmic backreaction over an extended redshift range
comment: Addendum to "Observational Tests for Distinguishing Classes of Cosmological Models'' (arXiv:2604.07244v1)
summary: In the recent preprint arXiv:2604.07244v1, the authors introduce a novel combination of redshift, distance, and expansion rate observables for constraining cosmic backreaction. The current work presents a first application of the method, yielding the first direct constraints on the total cosmic backreaction in our Universe over a significant redshift range. The constraints are consistent with vanishing backreaction within one standard deviation. However, the constraints are fairly weak and significant backreaction cannot be ruled out.

AI.tldr: First direct constraints on total cosmic backreaction using combined redshift-distance-expansion rate observables, consistent with zero within 1σ but too weak to rule out significant backreaction.
AI.motivation: To develop and apply a novel method for constraining cosmic backreaction effects in cosmology, providing the first direct observational constraints on this theoretical phenomenon over a significant redshift range.
AI.method: Combination of redshift, distance, and expansion rate observables to constrain cosmic backreaction, applied to observational data to obtain direct constraints on the total backreaction effect.
AI.result: First direct constraints on total cosmic backreaction show consistency with vanishing backreaction within one standard deviation, but constraints are fairly weak and cannot rule out significant backreaction effects.
AI.conclusion: The novel method successfully provides first direct observational constraints on cosmic backreaction, though current data yields weak constraints that are consistent with zero backreaction but cannot exclude potentially significant effects.

title: Kozai-driven mass loss of the circumbinary disk in D9 in orbit around the supermassive black hole Sgr A*
summary: The supermassive black hole (Sgr A*) in the Galactic center is surrounded by the S-star cluster consisting of young stars on eccentric orbits. Recently, the S-star binary, called D9, was found to be orbited by a circumbinary disk. Due to the gravitational interaction between Sgr A* and the binary, the disk could be short-lived. We investigate the evolution of the disk around a stellar binary while orbiting Sgr A*. We use the \texttt{AMUSE} framework for coupling a gravity solver (for the binary and Sgr. A*) with a hydrodynamics solver (for the disk). We find that, the disk eventually settles between 5.2$a_{\rm in}$ and 0.28 Hill radii of the binary. Here, $a_{\rm in}$ is the semi-major axis of D9. The inclination of the circumbinary disk follows the binary's, which evolves due to the von Zeipel-Lidov-Kozai (vZLK) mechanism induced by Sgr A*. The mean eccentricity of the disk is approximately in anti-phase with the eccentricity evolution of the binary. We find a vZLK timescale of $T_\text{vZLK}\approx62.5\,$kyr, which is two orders of magnitude shorter than the value reported by Peisker etal. (2024). As a consequence, D9 has undergone multiple vZLK oscillations in its lifetime of 2.7 Myr. We find the disk shows periodic bursts of mass loss on the vZLK timescale, suggesting that the mass loss itself is in part driven by the vZLK mechanism. The secular evolution observed in both the binary and the disk are consistent with theoretical predictions. We find the disk loses $\sim$7\% $\pm$ 2\% of its mass every vZLK cycle. If we extrapolate this mass loss, the disk will have 1\% of its current mass left after another $\sim$4 Myr. D9 will then be $\sim$6.7 Myr old, which is on the same order as the current average age of S cluster members. The vZLK-driven mass loss could, therefore, explain the absence of Br$γ$ emission from other S cluster members.

AI.tldr: The study investigates the evolution of a circumbinary disk around the D9 binary star in the Galactic center, finding that the von Zeipel-Lidov-Kozai mechanism from Sgr A* drives periodic mass loss from the disk, potentially explaining the absence of Brγ emission from other S cluster members.
AI.motivation: To understand the evolution and lifetime of circumbinary disks around S-star binaries in the Galactic center, particularly how gravitational interactions with the supermassive black hole Sgr A* affect disk stability and mass loss, which could explain observational features like the absence of Brγ emission from other S cluster members.
AI.method: Used the AMUSE framework to couple a gravity solver (for the binary and Sgr A*) with a hydrodynamics solver (for the disk), simulating the evolution of the circumbinary disk around the D9 binary while accounting for gravitational interactions with the central black hole.
AI.result: The disk settles between 5.2a_in and 0.28 Hill radii of the binary; disk inclination follows the binary's vZLK-driven evolution; disk eccentricity is anti-phase with binary eccentricity; vZLK timescale is ~62.5 kyr (two orders shorter than previous estimates); disk shows periodic mass loss bursts on vZLK timescale, losing ~7% ± 2% per cycle; extrapolation suggests disk will have 1% of current mass after ~4 Myr.
AI.conclusion: The vZLK mechanism induced by Sgr A* drives significant periodic mass loss from circumbinary disks around S-star binaries, potentially explaining the absence of Brγ emission from other S cluster members and suggesting these disks have limited lifetimes comparable to the age of S cluster stars.

title: Emergence of Complex Structures
summary: Complex structures often emerge from initially homogeneous or weakly correlated states. We address the apparent tension between this ordering and entropy growth through a unified framework combining semi-microscopic phase-space dynamics, transport geometry, information theory, and coarse-grained effective modeling. The key point is that entropy depends on the level of description: a coarse-grained spatial field may become more ordered as structure forms, even while the full phase-space description becomes more complex through shell crossing, multistreaming, and the activation of velocity degrees of freedom. Using a Lagrangian--Eulerian transport map, we show how density amplification is governed by the Jacobian of the deformation and how anisotropic collapse arises from the eigenvalues of a hierarchy of deformation tensors. Long-range interaction or information flow is encoded in the displacement field, so that nonlocality enters directly through transport. We connect this geometric description to a maximum-entropy Gaussian baseline and show how nonlinear transport and nonlocal coupling generate scale coupling, higher-order correlations, and non-Gaussianity. We then formulate a Landau--Ginzburg description in which the growth of seed anisotropies is interpreted as the activation of lower effective free-energy branches, providing a coarse-grained realization of self-organization. Applied to generated cosmological fields, this framework indicates that the nonlocal tidal level becomes relevant already at moderate overdensity. Although cosmological structure formation is the main realization considered here, the framework is intended more broadly as a mesoscopic language for systems in which transport, anisotropy, nonlocality, and self-organization are central.

AI.tldr: The paper presents a unified framework for understanding structure formation in complex systems, showing how apparent ordering emerges despite entropy growth through coarse-grained descriptions, transport geometry, and nonlocal interactions.
AI.motivation: To resolve the apparent tension between structure formation (ordering) and entropy growth in complex systems, particularly in cosmological structure formation but applicable more broadly to systems with transport, anisotropy, nonlocality, and self-organization.
AI.method: Combines semi-microscopic phase-space dynamics, transport geometry, information theory, and coarse-grained effective modeling using Lagrangian-Eulerian transport maps, deformation tensors, maximum-entropy Gaussian baselines, and Landau-Ginzburg descriptions.
AI.result: Shows that density amplification is governed by deformation Jacobians, anisotropic collapse by deformation tensor eigenvalues, and nonlocality enters through displacement fields. Demonstrates how nonlinear transport generates scale coupling, higher-order correlations, and non-Gaussianity, with nonlocal tidal effects becoming relevant at moderate overdensity.
AI.conclusion: Provides a mesoscopic framework explaining how coarse-grained ordering emerges despite microscopic entropy growth, with applications to cosmological structure formation and broader systems featuring transport, anisotropy, nonlocality, and self-organization.

title: Galactic Archaeology with the Subaru `Ōnohi`ula Prime Focus Spectrograph Strategic Program
comment: The Galactic Archaeology science case for the Subaru Strategic Program for the `Ōnohi`ula Prime Focus Spectrograph. Not yet submitted to any journal
summary: The recently commissioned Subaru `Ōnohi`ula Prime Focus Spectrograph (PFS) will obtain spectra from nearly 2,400 fibers that cover 1.24 square degrees. The 360 night Subaru Strategic Program for PFS is dedicating approximately one-third of its allocation (130 nights) to study the structure and evolution of galaxies in the Local Group. This Galactic Archaeological survey has three pillars. (1) We will determine whether the mass density profiles of dwarf galaxies are consistent with cusps, as expected for cold dark matter, or cores, as expected from alternative dark matter theories or baryonic feedback. We will deduce the density profiles as a function of radius from modeling of the full line-of-sight velocity and abundance distributions for six dwarf galaxies. Our total sample will consist of 18,000 member stars to beyond the nominal tidal radius of each system. (2) From measurements of the [alpha/Fe] abundance ratio, we will learn the difference in assembly history of the two most massive galaxies in the Local Group: M31 and the Milky Way. We will observe 30,000 member stars over 45 square degrees of M31's halo and outer disk. (3) We will uncover how the most fragile (outer) part of the Milky Way responded to accretion events both in the distant past (such as Gaia-Sausage Enceladus) and in more recent history (such as the Sagittarius dwarf spheroidal galaxy). To support this study, PFS will provide velocities and metallicities--from which, in combination with photometry, we will deduce ages--for tens of thousands of main-sequence stars out to a Galactocentric distance of ~30 kpc.

AI.tldr: The Subaru PFS Galactic Archaeology survey will use 130 nights to study Local Group galaxies through three main pillars: measuring dark matter profiles in dwarf galaxies, comparing M31 and Milky Way assembly histories via [alpha/Fe] ratios, and investigating the Milky Way's outer response to accretion events.
AI.motivation: To understand galaxy formation and evolution in the Local Group by addressing key questions about dark matter profiles in dwarf galaxies, differences in assembly history between M31 and the Milky Way, and the response of the Milky Way's outer regions to accretion events.
AI.method: Using the Subaru PFS with 2,400 fibers covering 1.24 square degrees to obtain spectra for: (1) 18,000 member stars in six dwarf galaxies to model velocity and abundance distributions; (2) 30,000 member stars over 45 square degrees of M31's halo and outer disk for [alpha/Fe] measurements; (3) tens of thousands of main-sequence stars out to ~30 kpc Galactocentric distance for velocities, metallicities, and ages.
AI.result: The survey will provide: (1) determination of whether dwarf galaxy mass density profiles have cusps (cold dark matter) or cores (alternative theories/baryonic feedback); (2) understanding of assembly history differences between M31 and Milky Way; (3) insights into how the Milky Way's outer regions responded to accretion events.
AI.conclusion: The PFS Galactic Archaeology survey represents a major observational program that will significantly advance our understanding of galaxy formation and evolution in the Local Group through comprehensive spectroscopic studies of dwarf galaxies, M31, and the Milky Way's outer regions.

title: Impact of Stochastic Pop~III X-ray Binaries on the Cosmological 21-cm Signal
summary: High-mass X-ray binaries are one of the primary drivers of the 21-cm signal from Cosmic Dawn and Reionization, playing a leading role in the thermal history of the intergalactic medium. In traditional semi-numerical simulations, a deterministic scaling relation between the total X-ray luminosity of high-mass X-ray binaries, $L_{\rm X}$, and star formation rate (SFR) is usually adopted. However, this assumption is inaccurate for high-redshift low-SFR regions hosting few sources. The spatial variation in the number and luminosity of these sources is expected to enhance fluctuations in the Cosmic Dawn 21-cm signal. Here we quantify this effect by introducing a stochastic $L_{\rm X}$ model sampled from a power-law X-ray luminosity function. Implementing this in 21cmSPACE, a large-scale simulation framework of Cosmic Dawn and Reionization, we find that the stochasticity leads to enhanced fluctuations in X-ray heating rate fields, and affects the 21-cm power spectrum on small scales ($k>0.3~ \mathrm{cMpc^{-1}}$). The impact of stochasticity on the global 21-cm signal and on the large-scale power spectrum is found to be negligible. Our results suggest these effects will remain undetected by the upcoming Square Kilometer Array. However, large-scale lunar-based experiments may be sensitive to the signatures of stochastic X-ray heating at $z\sim 25$. Quantifying these corrections is a vital step toward robust 21-cm modeling and ensuring that future precision data interpretation is free from astrophysical biases.

AI.tldr: Stochastic modeling of high-mass X-ray binaries enhances small-scale 21-cm fluctuations at Cosmic Dawn, but effects remain undetectable by SKA though potentially measurable by lunar-based experiments.
AI.motivation: Traditional deterministic scaling between X-ray luminosity and star formation rate is inaccurate for high-redshift, low-SFR regions with few sources, potentially biasing 21-cm signal predictions.
AI.method: Introduce stochastic L_X model sampled from power-law X-ray luminosity function, implement in 21cmSPACE simulation framework for Cosmic Dawn and Reionization.
AI.result: Stochasticity enhances X-ray heating rate fluctuations and affects 21-cm power spectrum on small scales (k>0.3 cMpc⁻¹), negligible impact on global signal and large-scale power spectrum.
AI.conclusion: Effects undetectable by SKA but potentially measurable by lunar-based experiments at z∼25; quantifying stochastic corrections is vital for robust 21-cm modeling and unbiased future data interpretation.

title: Environmental Dependence of Galaxy properties: A study of 341 Ring Galaxies in Cosmic Voids
summary: We investigate the morphological and physical properties of ring galaxies residing within cosmic voids. Using void catalogs from VoidFinder, ring candidates identified via the Galaxy Zoo 2 decision tree, and morphological classifications from the Buta (2017) CVRHS based catalog, we analyze a sample of 341 void ring galaxies and find a radial preference, with 91.5% located away from the void cores. Morphologically, inner rings and inner pseudorings account for 45.2% of the sample while outer pseudorings are even more common(56.3%) and outer rings appear in 17.9% of galaxies, which points to secular evolution driven by internal dynamics as the primary formation mechanism. Compared to the general void population, our sample ring galaxies are found to be more massive, redder, and have lower specific star formation rates. Subtle gradients in stellar mass and sSFR from void centers to edges also shows a gentle, density-dependent evolutionary progression. Our results show ring galaxies as a distinct, secularly evolved population shaped by the weakest large-scale environmental gradients

AI.tldr: Ring galaxies in cosmic voids show radial preference away from void cores, with morphological patterns indicating secular evolution driven by internal dynamics rather than environmental effects.
AI.motivation: To understand how ring galaxies form and evolve in the unique low-density environments of cosmic voids, where environmental influences are minimal, and to determine whether their formation is driven by internal dynamics or external factors.
AI.method: Used void catalogs from VoidFinder, identified ring candidates via Galaxy Zoo 2 decision tree, applied morphological classifications from Buta (2017) CVRHS catalog, and analyzed a sample of 341 void ring galaxies to study their spatial distribution, morphology, and physical properties compared to the general void population.
AI.result: 91.5% of void ring galaxies are located away from void cores. Morphologically, inner rings/pseudorings account for 45.2%, outer pseudorings 56.3%, and outer rings 17.9%. Ring galaxies are more massive, redder, and have lower specific star formation rates than the general void population, with subtle gradients in stellar mass and sSFR from void centers to edges.
AI.conclusion: Ring galaxies in cosmic voids represent a distinct, secularly evolved population primarily shaped by internal dynamics rather than environmental effects, with their properties showing gentle, density-dependent evolutionary progression across void environments.

title: Cosmological inference with halo clustering reconstructed from the redshift-space galaxy distribution
summary: Accurate modeling of small-scale redshift-space clustering is crucial for full shape RSD analyses, where satellite galaxies contribute to 1-halo terms and Finger-of-God distortions. We investigate halo reconstruction based on the cylinder grouping (CG) method of Okumura et al. (2017), which selects an effective halo center tracer from the observed galaxy distribution, and how it impacts cosmological parameter inference. Using DESI-like luminous red galaxy mock catalogs from the AbacusSummit simulations at $z=1.1$, we perform effective field theory (EFT)-based full-shape modeling of the power spectrum of the reconstructed-halo sample. We show that the dominant reconstruction-induced systematics can be described and incorporated within the standard EFT framework. In particular, a simple multipole-dependent rescaling inferred directly from the data on large scales captures the dominant effect, while residual small-scale changes are absorbed by the standard counterterm and stochastic sector, without introducing additional reconstruction-specific parameters. The reconstructed-halo sample yields unbiased constraints on cosmological parameters, including the growth rate $fσ_8$ and Alcock-Paczynski parameters. Compared to the galaxy sample, it enables both improved robustness and increased statistical precision: the inferred $fσ_8$ remains stable when extending the fit beyond $k_{\max}\simeq 0.2\,h\,{\rm Mpc}^{-1}$, with its uncertainty reduced by more than $20\%$.

AI.tldr: Halo reconstruction via cylinder grouping reduces redshift-space clustering systematics, enabling unbiased cosmological constraints with improved precision and robustness in full-shape RSD analyses.
AI.motivation: Accurate modeling of small-scale redshift-space clustering is essential for full shape RSD analyses, where satellite galaxies contribute to 1-halo terms and Finger-of-God distortions. Current methods need improvement to handle these systematics while maintaining cosmological parameter inference accuracy.
AI.method: Uses halo reconstruction based on the cylinder grouping (CG) method to select effective halo center tracers from observed galaxy distributions. Performs effective field theory (EFT)-based full-shape modeling of power spectra from reconstructed-halo samples using DESI-like luminous red galaxy mock catalogs from AbacusSummit simulations at z=1.1.
AI.result: Reconstruction-induced systematics can be described within standard EFT framework. Simple multipole-dependent rescaling captures dominant effects, while residual small-scale changes are absorbed by standard counterterm and stochastic sector without additional parameters. Reconstructed-halo sample yields unbiased constraints on fσ₈ and Alcock-Paczynski parameters, with fσ₈ uncertainty reduced by >20% and stability maintained beyond k_max ≈ 0.2 h/Mpc.
AI.conclusion: Halo reconstruction via cylinder grouping enables both improved robustness and increased statistical precision in cosmological parameter inference compared to galaxy samples, providing unbiased constraints with reduced systematics in full-shape RSD analyses.

title: Possible Supermassive Dark Object Composed of Light Fermionic Gas with an Embedded Neutron Star Core
summary: The structure of dark matter admixed neutron stars (DANSs) are investigated, adopting a non-annihilating self-interacting fermionic dark matter (DM) model, with a particular focus on the case of the light DM particle mass $m_D \in [10^{-10}, 1]$ GeV. The DANSs become DM-dominated configurations when $m_D <10^{-1}$ GeV, where a compact neutron star core becomes embedded within an extremely large DM halo. It is found that the maximum mass of DANSs is inversely proportional to $m_{ D}$, approximately as $ 0.627 (\mathrm{GeV/} m_{\rm D})^2 ~\mathrm{M_{\odot}}$, which implies that extremely large masses can be achieved for small $m_{\rm D}$. For $m_D \sim5\times10^{-4}$ GeV, the calculated mass and size of the DM halo can be comparable to those of supermassive black holes such as Sgr A*. Our findings hint at a scenario where neutron stars might serve as strong gravitational seeds for such supermassive dark objects.

AI.tldr: Dark matter admixed neutron stars with light fermionic dark matter (10^-10 to 1 GeV) can become DM-dominated with compact neutron cores inside huge DM halos, potentially explaining supermassive black hole-like objects.
AI.motivation: To investigate how non-annihilating self-interacting fermionic dark matter affects neutron star structure, particularly for light DM particles, and explore whether such configurations could explain supermassive dark objects like Sgr A*.
AI.method: Analyzed dark matter admixed neutron stars using a non-annihilating self-interacting fermionic dark matter model, focusing on light DM particle masses in the range 10^-10 to 1 GeV, examining how DM domination affects stellar structure.
AI.result: DANSs become DM-dominated when m_D < 10^-1 GeV, forming compact neutron cores within extremely large DM halos. Maximum mass scales inversely with m_D^2: ~0.627(GeV/m_D)^2 M⊙. For m_D ~5×10^-4 GeV, halo mass and size match supermassive black holes like Sgr A*.
AI.conclusion: Neutron stars with light fermionic dark matter could form DM-dominated configurations with supermassive black hole-like properties, suggesting neutron stars might serve as gravitational seeds for supermassive dark objects.

title: Starbursts at Cosmic Dawn: Formation of Globular Clusters, Ultra-Faint Dwarfs, and Population III star clusters at z > 6
comment: 153 pages, 27 figures. M.Sc. thesis defended in 2022 at Stockholm University (supervisor: Garrelt Mellema). For more recent modelling of the critical halo mass for star formation, and Ly$α$ stellar feedback, see arXiv:2303.08024 and arXiv:2409.19288, respectively. Original thesis can also be found at: https://www.diva-portal.org/smash/record.jsf?pid=diva2%3A1667717&dswid=-6362
summary:
In the standard model of cosmology ($Λ$CDM) the first stars, star clusters, and galaxies are expected to have formed in low-mass dark matter halos at high redshifts ($z \sim 6 - 30$). Attempts to predict the properties and abundances of these objects have mainly relied on numerically expensive cosmological simulations, which often lack the sub-parsec resolution needed to resolve compact star clusters and/or neglect potentially important stellar feedback processes. Motivated by this, I introduce Anaxagoras, a detailed analytical ab initio model of starbursts in low-mass halos. The model includes gas cooling, central gas accretion and disk formation, and stellar feedback from direct radiation pressure, Ly$α$ scattering and IR photons, stellar winds, expanding H II regions, and (crudely) supernovae.
  I apply Anaxagoras to star formation at $z > 6$ in satellite halos of the Milky Way, as well as to Population III (Pop III) star formation in minihalos. For the Milky Way setup, hundreds of galaxies are predicted to form with luminosities, half-mass radii, mass-to-light ratios, and ages in good agreement with the observed local population of Ultra-Faint Dwarfs. Furthermore, at least $\sim 40$ old globular cluster candidates with initial stellar masses $10^5 - 10^6\,M_\odot$ are predicted to form at the centers of low-mass halos. Finally, if Pop III stars are not overly massive ($25\,M_\odot$), between $\sim 1 - 30$ stars could form per minihalo at $z > 20$, increasing to $\sim 10 - 500$ at $z < 15$ as Lyman-Werner feedback delays star formation until halos reach larger masses; if Pop III stars are more massive ($140\,M_\odot$), most minihalos form just a single star.

AI.tldr: Anaxagoras is an analytical ab initio model for starbursts in low-mass halos at high redshifts, predicting Ultra-Faint Dwarf formation, globular cluster candidates, and Population III star formation patterns.
AI.motivation: Standard cosmological simulations lack sub-parsec resolution needed for compact star clusters and often neglect important stellar feedback processes, motivating development of a detailed analytical model.
AI.method: Anaxagoras analytical ab initio model includes gas cooling, central gas accretion, disk formation, and comprehensive stellar feedback (radiation pressure, Lyα scattering, IR photons, stellar winds, H II regions, supernovae). Applied to star formation at z > 6 in Milky Way satellite halos and Population III star formation in minihalos.
AI.result: For Milky Way satellites: hundreds of galaxies form with properties matching observed Ultra-Faint Dwarfs; ~40 old globular cluster candidates with 10^5-10^6 M⊙ form in low-mass halos. For Pop III: with 25 M⊙ stars, 1-30 stars per minihalo at z > 20, increasing to 10-500 at z < 15 due to Lyman-Werner feedback; with 140 M⊙ stars, most minihalos form single stars.
AI.conclusion: Anaxagoras successfully models early star formation in low-mass halos, reproducing observed dwarf galaxy populations and predicting globular cluster formation, while revealing how Pop III star mass affects multiplicity in minihalos.

title: A consistent MOND modelling of the Bullet Cluster
summary:
It is a common miss-conception that 1E 0657-56, the "Bullet Cluster", is somehow inconsistent with MOND expectations. The argument
  centres on the fact that the baryonic matter distribution of this system is dominated by the X-ray emitting gas, while the
  total projected surface density required under General Relativity to explain the observed lensing signal, centres on the observed galaxies.
  This is sometimes interpreted as being in conflict with MOND, as under such an interpretation, it is naively assumed that all
  dark matter being absent, the gravitational potential should necessarily be dominated by the largest mass distribution, that of
  the gas. However, just as under General Relativity, under MOND, the total gravitational potential of a system depends sensitively
  upon the volume density and not just on the total mass. It is shown in this {\it letter} that the surface density which QUMOND predicts will be inferred
  under a standard gravity framework from the total gravitational potential of the Bullet Cluster, closely matches what General
  Relativity inferences of lensing observations return. The close-to-point-like galaxies imply under QUMOND a relatively much larger
  surface density signal than what is expected from the Mpc scale gas distribution.

AI.tldr: The paper argues that the Bullet Cluster (1E 0657-56) is not inconsistent with MOND as commonly believed, showing that QUMOND predictions for inferred surface density match General Relativity lensing observations.
AI.motivation: To address the widespread misconception that the Bullet Cluster observations contradict Modified Newtonian Dynamics (MOND), specifically challenging the notion that the system's gravitational potential should be dominated by gas rather than galaxies under MOND.
AI.method: The authors use QUMOND (a quasi-linear formulation of MOND) to calculate the total gravitational potential of the Bullet Cluster system, considering both the volume density distribution of gas and the near-point-like galaxies, then determine what surface density would be inferred under standard gravity framework.
AI.result: QUMOND predicts that the inferred surface density from the total gravitational potential closely matches what General Relativity inferences from lensing observations return, showing that the Bullet Cluster is consistent with MOND expectations.
AI.conclusion: The Bullet Cluster is not evidence against MOND; the apparent discrepancy arises from misunderstanding how gravitational potential depends on volume density distribution in MOND, not just total mass. The near-point-like galaxies produce a relatively larger surface density signal than the diffuse gas distribution under QUMOND.

title: The Milky Way Tomography with Subaru Hyper Suprime-Cam. II. Global halo structure
comment: 14 pages, 10 figures, and 2 tables. Submitted to PASJ
summary: We investigate the structure of the Milky Way's stellar halo within 70 kpc of the Sun using a wide-field photometric catalog obtained from the Hyper Suprime-Cam (HSC) Subaru Strategic Program (HSC-SSP). We employ a large sample of main-sequence turn-off stars as distance tracers. To robustly derive the structural parameters of the stellar halo, we develop a forward-modeling framework that explicitly accounts for distance uncertainties, the solar position, and the limited sky coverage of the survey. Applying this method to the HSC-SSP catalog, we found that the smooth stellar halo is well described by a double power-law density profile, with inner and outer slope of approximately -3.3 and -4.8, respectively, with a break radius of 17.4 kpc. The outer steep density slope derived in this work supports a picture in which the present-day structure of the Milky Way's stellar halo is influenced by early massive accretion events, consistent with inferences from kinematic substructures such as Gaia Enceladus/Sausage. Ongoing wide-field imaging surveys, including UNIONS and LSST, will provide further constraints on the structure of the stellar halo and key insights into its formation history.

AI.tldr: The study analyzes the Milky Way's stellar halo structure within 70 kpc using HSC-SSP photometric data, finding a double power-law density profile with inner slope -3.3, outer slope -4.8, and break radius at 17.4 kpc, supporting early massive accretion events.
AI.motivation: To understand the structure of the Milky Way's stellar halo and constrain its formation history by deriving robust structural parameters from wide-field photometric data, addressing limitations of previous studies with incomplete sky coverage and distance uncertainties.
AI.method: Developed a forward-modeling framework using Hyper Suprime-Cam Subaru Strategic Program (HSC-SSP) photometric catalog with main-sequence turn-off stars as distance tracers. The method explicitly accounts for distance uncertainties, solar position, and limited sky coverage to robustly derive structural parameters.
AI.result: Found the smooth stellar halo is well described by a double power-law density profile: inner slope ≈ -3.3, outer slope ≈ -4.8, with break radius at 17.4 kpc. The steep outer slope supports influence of early massive accretion events, consistent with kinematic substructures like Gaia Enceladus/Sausage.
AI.conclusion: The derived steep outer density profile provides evidence for early massive accretion events shaping the Milky Way's stellar halo. Future wide-field surveys (UNIONS, LSST) will offer further constraints on halo structure and formation history.

title: Extragalactic microlensing through Ultra Diffuse Galaxies
comment: 11 pages, 4 figures. Submitted to Astrophysical Journal letter, comments welcomed
summary: Stellar microlensing is a powerful method to constrain compact dark matter models, uncover binary stars, and exoplanets during caustic crossing events. At cosmological distances, {\it James-Webb Space Telescope} ({\it JWST}) is routinely detecting microlensed giant stars in highly magnified galaxies behind massive lensing clusters. Here, we explore for the first time microlensing in modest redshift galaxies commonly seen through local Ultra Diffuse Galaxies (UDGs). Using the UDG NGC1052-DF2 as a case study, we found that detecting UDG microlensing events through UDGs is possible. However, a low total UDG microlensing event rate of $\sim 5.6\times10^{-2}\,\textrm{yr}^{-1}$ over its five background galaxies is expected for typical {\it JWST} $\sim 29\,$mag visits, and a low Vera Rubin Legacy Survey of Space and Time (LSST) detection rate of $\sim 2\times10^{-8}\,\textrm{yr}^{-1}$ such that NGC1052-DF2 might not be a prime target given its lack of low-redshift background galaxies. {\it Euclid} is ideal for identifying samples of low-redshift star-forming galaxies seen through local galaxies for deeper cadenced follow-up, where our zeroth-order calculation estimates that $\mathcal{O}(1-10)$ events per year are expected over the whole sky under the monitoring of LSST. Finally, we postulate that UDG microlensing will allow an independent estimate of the initial mass function (IMF) and the stellar multiplicity in the low mass regime, of considerable interest for UDG galaxies, where stellar mass has been claimed to predominate over dark matter in some cases, including NGC1052-DF2.

AI.tldr: Detection of microlensing events through Ultra Diffuse Galaxies (UDGs) is possible but has low event rates for current telescopes; Euclid could identify suitable targets for follow-up, potentially enabling IMF and stellar multiplicity studies in UDGs.
AI.motivation: To explore microlensing through modest redshift galaxies seen through local Ultra Diffuse Galaxies (UDGs), using NGC1052-DF2 as a case study, to assess detection feasibility and potential for studying stellar properties in UDGs where stellar mass may dominate over dark matter.
AI.method: Used NGC1052-DF2 as a case study to calculate microlensing event rates through UDGs, considering JWST and LSST capabilities, and performed zeroth-order calculations for Euclid's potential in identifying suitable low-redshift star-forming galaxies for cadenced follow-up.
AI.result: Detection of UDG microlensing events is possible but has low rates: ~5.6×10⁻² yr⁻¹ for JWST (~29 mag visits) over five background galaxies, and ~2×10⁻⁸ yr⁻¹ for LSST. Euclid could identify samples for follow-up, with O(1-10) events per year expected over the whole sky under LSST monitoring.
AI.conclusion: UDG microlensing offers potential for independent estimates of the initial mass function and stellar multiplicity in the low-mass regime, particularly relevant for UDGs where stellar mass may dominate over dark matter, though NGC1052-DF2 may not be optimal due to lack of low-redshift background galaxies.

title: The Milky Way Tomography with Subaru Hyper Suprime-Cam: Implications for the past orbit of the Large Magellanic Cloud
comment: 8 pages and 4 figures. Submitted to ApJL
summary: We report the discovery of diffuse stellar substructure in the Milky Way's outer halo toward Boötes, unveiled by deep imaging data of the Subaru/Hyper Suprime-Cam. This substructure is detected as an excess of faint main-sequence stars, at heliocentric distances beyond 30 kpc, extending over at least 100 $\mathrm{deg^2}$. To infer its origin, we compare the projected spatial distribution of these stars to that of simulated tidal debris from the Large Magellanic Cloud (LMC), under the assumptions that the LMC is on either its first or second passage of the Milky Way. We found that the observed overdensity lies in a region of the halo where debris from the LMC is expected if it is on its initial pericentric phase 7-8 Gyr ago, which is predicted in the second-passage model, while the first-passage model is unable to explain the observed substructure. Chemo-kinematical data are required to further constrain its past orbit and to understand the origin of this new halo substructure, as should be obtained in the near future with deep photometric surveys such as UNIONS and LSST, and wide-field spectroscopy such as possible with PFS and DESI.

AI.tldr: Discovery of diffuse stellar substructure in Milky Way's outer halo toward Boötes using Subaru/Hyper Suprime-Cam data, potentially linked to Large Magellanic Cloud tidal debris from a second passage scenario.
AI.motivation: To identify and characterize diffuse stellar substructures in the Milky Way's outer halo and understand their origins through comparison with simulated tidal debris from satellite galaxies.
AI.method: Used deep imaging data from Subaru/Hyper Suprime-Cam to detect faint main-sequence stars beyond 30 kpc, compared spatial distribution with simulated tidal debris from the Large Magellanic Cloud under first and second passage scenarios.
AI.result: Discovered diffuse stellar substructure extending over at least 100 deg² in Boötes direction; observed overdensity aligns with LMC debris predictions from second-passage model (7-8 Gyr ago pericentric phase), while first-passage model cannot explain the substructure.
AI.conclusion: The substructure likely originates from LMC tidal debris during its second passage, but requires chemo-kinematical data from future surveys (UNIONS, LSST, PFS, DESI) for definitive confirmation and orbital constraints.

title: Full-polarization millimeter wavelength variability of Sagittarius A* during the 2018 EHT campaign
summary: Sagittarius A* (Srg A*), the supermassive black hole at the center of the Milky Way, provides a unique laboratory to study accretion dynamics and plasma processes near the event horizon. We investigated the variability and polarization properties of Srg A* using ALMA observations during the 2018 Event Horizon Telescope campaign. We analyzed high-cadence full-polarization light curves from ALMA at millimeter wavelengths, performed time-series analysis, and investigated the temporal behavior during an X-ray flare observed by Chandra on 2018 April 24. The variability characteristics are compared with expectations from standard accretion flow models. We find low variability in total intensity ($σ/μ< 10\%$), but significantly higher variability in linear and circular polarization (~ 30% and ~ 50%, respectively). A time-series analysis reveals red-noise variability, with power spectral densities between -2 and -3 across all Stokes parameters. Polarized intensity shows stable intra-day timescales, while total intensity exhibits more variable timescales, suggesting distinct emission regions, with polarization likely arising from a coherent structure. On April 24, a statistically significant inter-band delay in polarized intensity coincides with a near-simultaneous X-ray and millimeter peak that deviates from the typical delayed flare scenario. This event also features enhanced millimeter variability and coherent polarization loop evolution. The observed simultaneity challenges standard models of transient synchrotron emission with cooling delays, favoring instead a scenario of continuous energy injection in an optically thin region. Our results offer new constraints on the physical mechanisms driving variability in Srg A*, and provide key observational input for refining theoretical models of accretion and plasma behavior in the vicinity of supermassive black holes.

AI.tldr: ALMA observations of Sagittarius A* reveal low total intensity variability but high polarization variability, with simultaneous X-ray and millimeter peaks challenging standard cooling delay models and favoring continuous energy injection.
AI.motivation: Sagittarius A* provides a unique laboratory to study accretion dynamics and plasma processes near the event horizon, particularly during the 2018 Event Horizon Telescope campaign to understand variability mechanisms.
AI.method: Analyzed high-cadence full-polarization light curves from ALMA at millimeter wavelengths, performed time-series analysis, and investigated temporal behavior during an X-ray flare observed by Chandra on 2018 April 24.
AI.result: Found low total intensity variability (σ/μ<10%) but significantly higher linear (~30%) and circular (~50%) polarization variability. Red-noise variability with PSD slopes between -2 and -3 across all Stokes parameters. Polarized intensity shows stable intra-day timescales while total intensity exhibits more variable timescales. On April 24, observed statistically significant inter-band delay in polarized intensity coinciding with near-simultaneous X-ray and millimeter peak.
AI.conclusion: The observed simultaneity challenges standard models of transient synchrotron emission with cooling delays, favoring a scenario of continuous energy injection in an optically thin region. Results provide new constraints on physical mechanisms driving variability in Sgr A* and key observational input for refining theoretical models of accretion and plasma behavior near supermassive black holes.

title: Vertical Structure of Local Disk Galaxies revealed by DESI Imaging Data
comment: 9 pages,6 figures,accepted for publication in ApJ
summary: The vertical structure of galactic disks is an important probe of disk assembly history. We investigate a sample of 79 local disk galaxies within 50 Mpc using data from the DESI Legacy Imaging Surveys. Vertical luminosity profiles as a function of radius in the g, r, and z bands are extracted and fitted with a single-component sech^2 model to determine the scale height and its radial variation (flaring). Our results show that local galactic disks are generally thin with negligible flaring. The median scale heights at one effective radius are 0.21, 0.22, and 0.22 kpc in the g, r, and z bands, respectively, while the corresponding median radial gradients are -0.006, 0.003, and 0.001. These values are consistent with those of the geometric thin disk of the Milky Way, represented by metal-rich, low-[alpha/Fe] populations, supporting the conclusion of weak flaring. We also find a clear positive correlation between scale height and stellar mass, extending down to 10^7 solar masses. These results provide a homogeneous benchmark for the vertical structure of nearby disk galaxies and support the cosmological representativeness of the Milky Way thin disk.

AI.tldr: Local disk galaxies show thin vertical profiles with negligible flaring, consistent with Milky Way's thin disk, and scale height correlates positively with stellar mass.
AI.motivation: To investigate the vertical structure of galactic disks as a probe of disk assembly history and establish a homogeneous benchmark for nearby disk galaxies.
AI.method: Analyzed 79 local disk galaxies within 50 Mpc using DESI Legacy Imaging Surveys data, extracted vertical luminosity profiles in g, r, and z bands, fitted with single-component sech^2 model to determine scale height and radial variation (flaring).
AI.result: Local galactic disks are generally thin with negligible flaring: median scale heights at one effective radius are 0.21, 0.22, and 0.22 kpc in g, r, and z bands respectively, with median radial gradients of -0.006, 0.003, and 0.001. Clear positive correlation found between scale height and stellar mass down to 10^7 solar masses.
AI.conclusion: Results provide homogeneous benchmark for vertical structure of nearby disk galaxies and support cosmological representativeness of Milky Way thin disk, indicating weak flaring in local galactic disks.

title: Apparent Stability in Self-Gravitating Turbulence and the Evolution of Molecular Clouds
summary: Recent observations of hydrostatic structure and virial equilibrium in supersonically turbulent, self-gravitating molecular clouds imply a stability that contrasts with the transcience of turbulent structure. To investigate this contradiction, we model a molecular cloud as a turbulent eddy and study its evolution as a dynamical system. In a two-dimensional phase space of structure and energy, we find that the dynamical equilibrium is a saddle point, stable in the direction aligned with force balance, but unstable in the direction of energy balance because of the combination of the turbulent dissipation and the negative heat capacity of self-gravitation. Near the saddle point, evolutionary trajectories follow a characteristic pattern that first approaches the equilibrium before departing in the direction of instability. Since the phase-space speed is proportional to the virial and energy imbalance, trajectories slow near the equilibrium resulting in a local overdensity of clouds. Also, near equilibrium, the relaxation to force balance is faster than the growth rate of the instability in energy. Consequently, more clouds are observed in near equilibrium states with hydrostatic structure even though the equilibrium is metastable. This resolves the apparent contradiction of equilibrium structure observed in dynamically unstable, self-gravitating turbulence.

AI.tldr: Molecular clouds appear stable despite turbulent dynamics because their equilibrium is a saddle point - stable in force balance but unstable in energy balance, creating a local overdensity of clouds near equilibrium.
AI.motivation: To resolve the contradiction between observed hydrostatic structure/virial equilibrium in molecular clouds and the transient nature of turbulent structure in these self-gravitating systems.
AI.method: Model molecular cloud as a turbulent eddy and study its evolution as a dynamical system in a two-dimensional phase space of structure and energy, analyzing equilibrium stability and evolutionary trajectories.
AI.result: The dynamical equilibrium is a saddle point: stable along force balance direction but unstable along energy balance direction due to turbulent dissipation and negative heat capacity of self-gravitation. Trajectories slow near equilibrium, creating local overdensity of clouds, with faster relaxation to force balance than instability growth.
AI.conclusion: Molecular clouds are observed near equilibrium despite dynamical instability because the equilibrium is metastable (saddle point), with trajectories spending more time near equilibrium due to slower phase-space speed, explaining apparent contradiction of equilibrium structure in unstable turbulence.

title: Systematic census of RR Lyrae stars in Milky Way stellar streams
summary: Context. Nearly 150 tidal streams are known in the Milky Way, but full phase-space information exists for only a few. RR Lyrae stars (RRL), as standard candles, provide a powerful way to probe these structures, yet they have been identified in less than a dozen streams. Aims. We study the RRL population in all known stellar streams with reported proper motions in the galstreams library, performing the first systematic census of these stars. Our goals are to identify likely RRL members, map distances along streams, and compare RRL populations in streams and their progenitors. Method. We use a union of the largest RRL catalogs (Gaia DR3 SOS, PS1, and ASAS-SN-II) to construct a Bayesian probabilistic membership model and find 361 RRL in the 56 streams studied. Results. i) We find that 32 of the 56 streams have RRL in their tidal tails -- 13 with progenitors and 19 without; 13 of these contain more than 3 RRL in their tails. ii) We report new RRL detections in 31 of these streams, anchoring distances and, in particular, inferring new distance gradients for 5 of them. iii) Our method provides intrinsic dispersion estimates in distance and proper motion for each track and statistically quantifies the expected contamination. iv) The census revealed some complex origin histories, such as the new plausible origin scenario we propose for M92 with multiple progenitors. v) We find that the presence of RRL in the tidal tails is linked to the late stages of progenitor dissolution. Conclusions. This census represents a first step toward identifying which of the studied stellar streams contain a significant number of RRL based on currently reported tracks while also providing a homogeneous and robust catalog of RRL members with precise empirical distances, crucial for a full phase-space analysis of these structures and their use as probes of the Galaxy's history and gravitational potential.

AI.tldr: First systematic census of RR Lyrae stars in 56 Milky Way stellar streams identifies 361 RRL members, reveals 32 streams contain RRL in tidal tails, provides new distance measurements and gradients, and links RRL presence to late-stage progenitor dissolution.
AI.motivation: Despite nearly 150 known tidal streams in the Milky Way, full phase-space information exists for only a few. RR Lyrae stars as standard candles can probe these structures, but have been identified in less than a dozen streams, necessitating a systematic census.
AI.method: Used union of largest RRL catalogs (Gaia DR3 SOS, PS1, ASAS-SN-II) to construct Bayesian probabilistic membership model for 56 streams with reported proper motions in galstreams library, identifying 361 RRL members.
AI.result: Found RRL in 32 of 56 streams (13 with progenitors, 19 without); 13 streams contain >3 RRL; new detections in 31 streams; new distance gradients for 5 streams; intrinsic dispersion estimates for distance/proper motion; revealed complex origin histories like M92 with multiple progenitors; linked RRL presence to late-stage progenitor dissolution.
AI.conclusion: First systematic census provides homogeneous catalog of RRL members with precise empirical distances, crucial for full phase-space analysis of stellar streams and their use as probes of Galaxy's history and gravitational potential.

title: The high-altitude, inner-disc, and chemically peculiar open cluster UBC 1052
comment: 23 pages (15 pages main text, 8 pages appendix) and 15 figures. Accepted for publication in Astronomy & Astrophysics
summary: Out of all the discovered open clusters (OCs) that are located in the inner part of the Galaxy, only a small fraction has been observed with high-resolution spectroscopy. An intriguing population of inner-disc OCs at relatively high altitudes ($Z$) from the Galactic plane remains poorly studied. There are few reliable detections of such OCs, and their occurrence rate, dynamical origin and survival mechanism remain uncertain. We perform a detailed spectroscopic analysis of UBC 1052, located at a cylindrical galactocentric radius $R_{GC} = 6.1$ kpc and $Z = 340$ pc, which stands out as the oldest and highest-|$Z$| inner-disc OC studied at high resolution to date. We used FLAMES/VLT to acquire high signal-to-noise ratio UVES spectra of four red clump (RC) members ($G\sim14$ mag). From them we derived high-precision radial velocities ($v_{r}$) and local thermodynamic equilibrium chemical abundances for 23 elements through a strict line-by-line differential analysis, achieving a median precision in [X/H] of $\simeq0.06$ dex for each star. The four RC stars have fully compatible chemical abundances, with [X/H] dispersions among them <$0.03$ dex for 20 elements. We also acquired GIRAFFE spectra of other candidate members and derived their $v_{r}$. We find that UBC 1052 has an age of $2.25\pm0.25$ Gyr, a distance of $3.11\pm0.07$ kpc, an extinction $A_{V} =1.23$ mag, a mean radial velocity of $34.0\pm0.6$ $km$ ${s}^{-1}$, and a slightly super-solar [Fe/H] = $0.05\pm0.01$ dex. Such relatively low [Fe/H] at its $R_{GC}$ suggests that UBC 1052 is a rare candidate for an inward-migrated OC in the inner disc. Its detailed abundance pattern (e.g. [Ba/Zr] and [Nd/Y]) shows some interesting features that appear to be unique in the current census of OCs studied at high resolution, making it an interesting object for potential strong chemical-tagging searches for already dispersed member stars. [Abridged]

AI.tldr: High-resolution spectroscopic analysis reveals UBC 1052 as an old, high-altitude inner-disc open cluster with unique chemical signatures, suggesting inward migration and potential for chemical tagging studies.
AI.motivation: To investigate the poorly studied population of inner-disc open clusters at high altitudes from the Galactic plane, focusing on UBC 1052 as the oldest and highest-Z inner-disc cluster studied at high resolution.
AI.method: Used FLAMES/VLT to acquire high-SNR UVES spectra of four red clump members, performing line-by-line differential analysis for precise radial velocities and chemical abundances of 23 elements; supplemented with GIRAFFE spectra for additional candidate members.
AI.result: UBC 1052 has age 2.25±0.25 Gyr, distance 3.11±0.07 kpc, extinction A_V=1.23 mag, mean radial velocity 34.0±0.6 km/s, and slightly super-solar [Fe/H]=0.05±0.01 dex; shows unique abundance patterns with low [Fe/H] for its galactocentric radius, suggesting inward migration.
